clue.text: Support excellent social event

blocks.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate
a dance is a social gathering

explanation.surface: Someone backs a really good party.
explanation.definitionFit: Aidance is an old noun for help or assistance, a synonym of support.

clue.text: A goddess to beguile

blocks.note: taken as written
the Muses were the nine goddesses of the arts

explanation.surface: A goddess sets out to charm someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to entertain or divert them, close to the sense of beguiling them.

clue.text: Gave lots of colour to former journalist's claim

blocks.note: the claim is put in the speaker's own mouth: I'M
past means former, as in past president
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A retired journalist is said to have painted a vivid picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The ex-editor's claim is 'I'm past ED', read straight through as IMPASTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To impaste is to lay paint on thickly, so an impasted canvas was given heavy colour.

clue.text: Vibration of daughter, lass no good

indicators.note: no good means the abbreviation for good is taken away from the word before it

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a lass is a girl
G stands for good

explanation.surface: A daughter's restlessness is blamed on a badly behaved girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Dirl is a Scots word, so expect a dictionary check.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, a dirl is a thrill or tremor, a vibrating or ringing sensation.

clue.text: Grandparent's no longer adult very important

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
vital means essential

explanation.surface: An elderly relative no longer counts as a grown-up but is still treasured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' marks the definition as obsolete: avital once meant of a grandfather, that is, ancestral.
explanation.definitionFit: Avital, from Latin avus for grandfather, is an archaic adjective meaning ancestral or belonging to a grandparent.

clue.text: Suffering more as athlete in the heat? Crowd support needed

definitions.text: Suffering more as athlete in the heat?

blocks.note: to cram is to crowd together
a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: A runner flagging in hot weather needs the spectators behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Crampier is the comparative of crampy, so an athlete with worse muscle spasms in heat is crampier.

clue.text: Relationship of power that restricts little American nerd

indicators.note: something that restricts hems in what follows, holding it inside

blocks.note: the decibel expresses a ratio between two powers
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A power relationship constrains a small American.
explanation.walkthrough: D(WEE)B: the decibel is a logarithmic measure comparing two power levels.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is US slang for a boring, socially awkward person, a near synonym of nerd.

clue.text: Always getting stick in lift when one isn't working

indicators.note: to stick one thing in another is to insert it

blocks.note: to doff a hat is to lift it
ay (aye) is a poetic word for always

explanation.surface: Someone always gets criticised in the elevator for slacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like a noun, criticism, but 'getting stick in' tells you to insert.
explanation.definitionFit: A day off is a holiday from work, the time when someone is not on duty.

clue.text: In Chinese practice not all show us humanity (5, two words)

indicators.note: not all of the following phrase is used, only a stretch from inside it

blocks.note: the run starts at the last letter of the first word and ends two letters into the third

explanation.surface: Chinese custom, a sceptic says, does not always display compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Wushu is the Chinese term for the martial arts, practised as exercise and sport.

clue.text: A tree tangled up, one with round fruit

indicators.note: something tangled up is twisted out of its proper order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
Roman numeral one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A tree is snarled up with one bearing round fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An etaerio is an aggregate fruit, such as a raspberry, formed from many small fruitlets.

clue.text: Busy type with hot temper in the drinks industry

blocks.note: the busy bee of the saying
rage is violent anger

explanation.surface: A busy, hot-headed worker is employed by the drinks trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The beerage is a jocular term, modelled on peerage, for brewers collectively and the brewing trade.

clue.text: Movement in painting surprisingly rare with tight content

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the word appears in an unexpected order
here with means holding, as a content held within
content is what sits inside something, so this word goes in the middle

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taut means stretched tight

explanation.surface: A rare movement in painting has a tense subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Art autre, French for other art, was a 1950s abstract movement related to Tachisme and art informel.

clue.text: Rebellion in university — Paris trounced by Left

indicators.note: a team trounced is knocked about, so these letters are beaten into a new order

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
the letters to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A student revolt in which Paris is beaten by the Left.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Paris student uprising of 1968.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisal is an old word for an uprising, that is, a rebellion or revolt.

clue.text: What sounds like containers made of fabric or paper

indicators.note: what sounds like asks for a word said the same as the phrase that follows

blocks.clueFragment: containers made of fabric or paper
blocks.note: bags of cloth or paper are sacks

explanation.surface: A riddle asking for a word that resembles cloth or paper bags.
explanation.walkthrough: The final word does double duty: it ends the description of the bags and also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxe is a kind of albumenised photographic printing paper, named after Saxony.

clue.text: Witty remark about army officer

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: to remark is to say
Lt is short for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A clever quip is made about a military officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Witty remark' reads as one phrase, but the definition is the adjective alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Salty talk is racy and sharp, so salty can mean pungently witty or earthy.

clue.text: Heroic struggling — one won't succeed alone

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters writhe into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A heroic battle that no lone fighter can win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' looks like 'win' but means inherit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coheir shares an inheritance with others, so does not succeed to it by themselves.

clue.text: Some castle's carpenter works in part of the fortifications

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the words that follow is used

blocks.note: the run starts at the final e of the first word and takes the first four letters of the second

explanation.surface: A castle's woodworker repairs part of the defences.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarp, or scarp, is the steep inner bank of a defensive ditch.

clue.text: Chap is able to perform, fading away

blocks.note: a chap is a man
can means is able to
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: A man who can still perform is nonetheless losing his powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mancando is an Italian musical direction meaning dying away, decreasing in volume and pace.

clue.text: One acted in play providing pithy narrative

indicators.note: letters in play are moving about freely rather than staying fixed

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor's stage role gives them a good story to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short entertaining account of an incident, a brief story.

clue.text: Part of body in church in Tours

indicators.note: the second in places the church inside the travel word

blocks.note: tours are trips
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A body part is displayed in a church in the French city of Tours.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter dresses tours up as the French city; it is simply plural trips.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: See track with one left out on a wing

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so this letter is dropped from the word beside it

blocks.note: Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see
a trail is a track
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Look at a path where someone was abandoned on the flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not look but a diocese, ELY being the crossword's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Elytral relates to an elytron, the hardened forewing case of a beetle, so it describes something on a wing.

clue.text: French songstress coming to her conclusion with good moving on the spot

blocks.note: Edith Piaf, the French singer
fin is French for end, fitting a French singer
G stands for good

explanation.surface: Edith Piaf reaches the end of her life well, still moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Piaffing is the dressage movement in which a horse trots in place without moving forward.

clue.text: No longer shining and fresh, having to admit fortune half gone

indicators.note: half gone means only the first half of the word survives
to admit someone is to let them in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: fresh means recent
fortune is luck

explanation.surface: Something has lost its fresh shine and half its value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete word, so the definition is not 'dull'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relucent is an archaic adjective meaning shining or reflecting light, now out of use.

clue.text: Worthless sort of cow

blocks.note: first meaning: shoddy, of poor quality
second meaning: a dialect name for a cow with crumpled horns

explanation.walkthrough: Crummie is a Scots name for a cow with crooked horns, which the dictionary also spells as the slang word for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means shabby or inferior, and in Scots names a cow with bent horns.

clue.text: Church singer to quiver? Mass must be avoided

indicators.note: what must be avoided is kept out, so that letter goes missing

blocks.note: to quiver is to tremble
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A nervous choirboy shakes but tries to keep away from the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests the church service; it is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy soprano, the highest voice in a church choir.

clue.text: Evasive manoeuvre in miner's working area?

blocks.note: first meaning: a delaying tactic to avoid acting
second meaning: the space in a coal mine where a miner works the face

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the coal-mining sense, a less familiar meaning of a common word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means playing for time, and in mining it is the chamber where coal is cut.

clue.text: Old Mark and Bill in horse-drawn vehicle

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a cart is pulled by a horse
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: An old man named Mark and one called Bill ride in a horse cart.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark and Bill look like two men's names; Mark is the definition and Bill is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Caract is an obsolete spelling of character, in the sense of a distinctive sign or mark.

clue.text: The first person about to be entertained by one bird or another

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so this word is read the other way
a guest entertained by a host is held inside their home

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
we is the first person plural

explanation.surface: The first person spots one bird, then a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bare 'another', meaning another bird; 'one bird' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tewit is a dialect name for the lapwing, a different bird from the tit.

clue.text: Bed of no use whatever for fish

blocks.note: cott is an old spelling of cot, a small bed
US is slang shorthand for useless

explanation.surface: A bed that is completely useless for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottus is the genus of freshwater sculpins, including the bullhead, so it names a fish.

clue.text: Old torch placed on a small support, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken version, so take the sound not the spelling

blocks.note: in golf, a ball set on a tee is teed

explanation.surface: An antique torch is set on a little stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Teade, or tead, is an archaic word for a torch, used by Spenser.

clue.text: Ploughs once used in part of Northern Ireland

blocks.note: first meaning: primitive scratch ploughs
second meaning: the peninsula and former district in County Down

explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' reads as if the ploughs were used there; it just joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An ard is an early light plough, and the Ards Peninsula lies east of Strangford Lough.

clue.text: Wild animal in grass rolling over, acting

indicators.note: rolling over turns something end to end, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: rye is a cereal grass
A is short for acting, as in an acting rank

explanation.surface: A wild creature rolls about in the grass, putting on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyra is the reddish form of the jaguarundi, a wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Bishop involved in what could be Oxford dispute — it's hairy

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it

blocks.note: Oxford is a university, and a dispute is a row
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is mixed up in an Oxford quarrel, and things get dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's hairy' sounds like slang for risky, but means literally covered in hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A unibrow is a single continuous eyebrow, a strip of hair joining both brows.

clue.text: Mad ploys to divert from what traditional church choirs sing?

indicators.note: to divert something is to send it off its course, so these letters change order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild schemes to distract the church choir from its usual repertoire.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalmody is the singing of psalms, the staple of traditional choral worship.

clue.text: Outrush of gum

blocks.note: first meaning: a sudden charge out, as from a besieged fort
second meaning: an Australian name for certain eucalyptus trees

explanation.walkthrough: 'gum' is the gum tree, not chewing gum: in Australia various eucalypts are called sallies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sortie from a defended position, and also a eucalypt such as the snow gum.

clue.text: Medical manipulator may want to get this plant

definitions.text: Medical manipulator may want to get this

blocks.clueFragment: Medical manipulator may want to get this
blocks.note: first meaning: read as two words, what a bonesetter aims to achieve
second meaning: a North American herb of the daisy family

explanation.surface: An osteopath may want to acquire a certain herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it is the goal of anyone who treats fractures.
explanation.definitionFit: Boneset is the herb Eupatorium perfoliatum, once used in folk medicine, and a set bone is a fracture properly aligned.
